title: Dive Club, as models
status_note: Working research: models run locally, closed, and not yet shown to Ridd and Tommy.
oneliner: Two Dive Club hosts as persona models with a fast decision head.
role: I scraped, transcribed, diarized, trained and evaluated all of it myself, on one RTX 3060.

hero.alt: Reference image from the Dive Club studio.

media.alt: Bar chart of accuracy on 656 questions: Kev 0.811, Ridd 0.805, Tommy 0.811, Primeagen 0.834.
media.caption: The decision module keeps its accuracy when the backbone becomes a person.

body: I trained a small language model on each of Ridd's and Tommy's own speech from 317 public Dive Club episodes, then put a fast decision module on top. The studio lets you ask them questions; every line there is a curated, labeled synthetic line.

To get there I downloaded the episodes, transcribed them with Whisper, and diarized who said what, then trained one LoRA per host on Qwen3.5-4B-Base. Held-out perplexity dropped for both, so the voice transferred.

The honest part: judgment did not transfer. The model sounds like them but does not know what they would decide. The decision module did survive the backbone swap, 0.805 and 0.811 against 0.811 for plain Kev on 656 questions.
Models, weights and data stay closed until Ridd and Tommy say yes.
